evidence: The new `case "prose_pending":` printer arm had no printer-level test; 6d20383 adds TestPrintSyncPullPayloadProsePendingText asserting origin/master, `text conflict`, and `lit sync reconcile` in the rendered output.
guidance_note: When adding a new arm to a payload printer, add a test that drives the printer with that payload, not just the builder.

evidence: The inner `switch rec.State` had no default, so an unmapped reconcile state would leave result.State as "" and the CLI default would render it as ok; 6d20383 adds loud defaults to both the reconcile and receive switches.
guidance_note: When mapping one string-typed enum onto another, write the default arm that errors on an unmapped value in the same edit as the cases.

evidence: The hook's doc said it replaced UpByOne 'in applyPendingMigrations' while the check sat in the shared upByOne that liftWorkingSetToRegistry also calls. Accepting was right, but the agent took the comment-only option. The WARNING comment it wrote in 6d20383 then drew F15, and 92af94b deleted that comment and moved the hook into applyPendingMigrations.
guidance_note: When moving a test-injection hook into a stepper that now has a second caller, keep the hook at the one caller that needs it rather than documenting that it poisons both.

evidence: PruneMatching runs after `DOLT_RESET --hard mergedCommit`, so `return fmt.Errorf("prune reconcile snapshots...")` reported a committed merge as failed. 6a0cae3 writes the failure to stderr instead. The flag is a false positive: 6d20383 did not touch sync_reconcile.go, so the prune-return was original PR code.
guidance_note: When ordering post-commit housekeeping after a durable mutation, make its failure non-fatal and loud, matching the file's existing cleanup helpers.

evidence: SyncReceive and SyncReconcile each took the commit lock separately, so a window existed between them. The reviewer's trigger, 'a push from another machine', only matters if the reconcile refetches, and the packet does not show that it does; a local concurrent writer is the plausible trigger. Wrapping both in one reentrant withCommitLock (6a0cae3) closes it at low cost. The flag is a false positive: 6d20383 only added default arms.
guidance_note: When composing two independently-locked store operations into one logical operation, hold one lock across both from the start.

evidence: SyncPullResult lives in internal/store, and the reviewer concedes 'the CLI handles the change correctly' and that 'this is an internal package'. The only consumer, buildSyncPullPayload, was updated in the same PR, so there is no break to fix. The flag is a false positive: the struct change is original PR code.

Only the diverged/schema-skew paths of SyncPull were exercised; 6a0cae3 adds TestSyncPullStateTransitions with real up_to_date, fast_forwarded (asserting the lane edit was adopted), ahead and never_synced subtests. The flag is a false positive: the SyncPull mapping is original PR code.
guidance_note: When introducing a state-mapping function, write one store-level test per output state before opening the PR.

evidence: Only TestBuildSyncPullPayloadLinearizedIsOK covered the shared default arm; faadf85 replaces it with a four-state table test. The round-1 summary had already raised this as an advisory without an inline comment, and the agent did not act on it until round 2. The flag is a false positive: 6a0cae3 touched only store files, not cli/sync.go.
guidance_note: Act on advisories in the review summary body, not only on inline threads; this gap was named in round 1's summary.

evidence: The verbose ok path now prints `pulled remote/branch (state)` and no test set verbose=true; faadf85 adds TestPrintSyncPullPayloadVerboseOKShowsState over all four ok states. The flag is a false positive: the printer change is original PR code.
guidance_note: When changing an output format, test every mode flag (verbose and non-verbose) that reaches the changed line.

evidence: F2 had named the exact downstream symptom: 'The CLI's buildSyncPullPayload default branch would render it as "status":"ok"'. The F2 fix added loud defaults only in store.SyncPull and left the renderer's catch-all default. faadf85 enumerates the four ok states and makes the default emit status unknown.
guidance_note: When adding a loud default to one switch over an enum, grep every switch over that same enum (renderers included) and give each the same default.

evidence: newSnapshotGuard was constructed inside reconcileFromAnchors, which runs under retryTransientGCContention, so each retry took a fresh snapshot. faadf85 constructs the guard once in reconcile() and passes it in, so ensure() caches a single snapshot. The flag is a false positive: the guard placement is original PR code.
guidance_note: When placing a one-shot side effect, check whether the enclosing function is wrapped in a retry loop and hoist the effect's owner above it.

evidence: The reviewer itself calls the four provider constructions 'functionally correct but unnecessary'. Reconcile is a rare divergence-only path, and the three exports are at different anchor commits, so a single lift cannot be reused for all of them. Caching would add lifecycle state for no measurable gain.

The agent cites `FOREIGN KEY ... ON DELETE CASCADE` on issue_events and issue_event_changes, so `DELETE FROM issues` clears events before the replay. The assertion faadf85 added (totalEvents>0 and totalEvents==distinctEvents after the reconcile) would fail if the claimed collision or duplication occurred. The bug claim is wrong; the missing coverage was real and was added.

A migration-vs-downgrade symmetry test existed, but nothing covered the third classifier this PR added; 92af94b adds TestIsReconcileSnapshotNameDisjoint over all pairs. The flag is a false positive: faadf85 did not touch the classifier.
guidance_note: When adding a new member to a set of classifiers that must stay disjoint, extend the existing disjointness test to the new member in the same commit.

evidence: The reviewer says the WARNING comment added for F3 'mitigates it, but the structural risk remains'. Instead of the suggested caller discriminator, 92af94b makes upByOne pure and wraps the hook in a local `step` closure inside applyPendingMigrations, which removes the coupling F3's fix had only documented.
guidance_note: When a finding offers 'document it or split it', pick the structural fix if it is a few lines; a WARNING comment that explains a hazard invites the next round.

evidence: assertWorkingSetClean was applied to the prose-pending and schema-skew tests but not to the linearized one, which is the only outcome that mutates the data branch; 92af94b adds it there. The flag is a false positive: faadf85 did not touch that test.
guidance_note: When introducing a property assertion helper, apply it to every outcome the property is claimed for, starting with the mutating one.

evidence: `result.Ahead, result.Behind = rec.Ahead, rec.Behind` carries the pre-reconcile counts into a linearized result; f914fd7 re-reads SyncFreshness. The flag is a false positive: that line was original PR code, which 6a0cae3 only re-indented inside withCommitLock. The problem is a stale value, not a swallowed error, so no-silent-failure does not apply.
guidance_note: When a branch mutates state, recompute every derived field the result reports from the post-mutation state, not the pre-mutation snapshot.

evidence: The reviewer and the agent both say goose returns ErrNoNextVersion at the end and that (nil,nil) is undocumented; the packet does not show goose's contract, so whether this guard is real hardening or a defensive guard against an impossible state is unsettled. The reviewer noted the same loop shape in applyPendingMigrations, but the agent guarded only the lift loop. The flag is a false positive: the loop is original PR code.

narrative: Five rounds, mostly fresh advisory coverage gaps the reviewer surfaced in pre-existing PR code; the ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flags were nearly all false positives because a comment anchors to the head commit. Two fixes cost later findings: the loud default added for F2 was not swept to the CLI renderer's default (F10), and the comment-only fix for F3 drew the structural objection F15, after which the hook was moved. Each round also contained unrelated findings, so no round was purely avoidable.
guidance_observations: The round-1 summary named the buildSyncPullPayload coverage gap as an advisory, but it was acted on only once it became an inline thread in round 2; read summary-level advisories as findings.

Most rounds were driven by the reviewer finding new test-coverage gaps in original code; writing one test per enum output state and per mode flag before opening the PR would have removed F7, F8, F9 and F16.

evidence: The Dockerfile comment asserted that `COPY --from=darwin-toolchain /opt/macos-sdk` preserves a directory symlink, and nothing in the packet backs that. Replacing it with `RUN ln -s "/opt/MacOSX${MACOS_SDK_VERSION}.sdk" /opt/macos-sdk` (visible in f5e0ae9 in the #296 packet) is deterministic and single-copy whatever COPY does. The reviewer's [LAW:no-defensive-null-guards] tag was irrelevant, but the concern was not.
guidance_note: When a stage needs a symlink produced in another stage, recreate it with `ln -s` in the consuming stage instead of copying the link.

narrative: One round with one advisory about a cross-stage symlink COPY. The agent replaced it with `ln -s` and the PR merged. The finding was in original PR code.

evidence: The premise is correct: os.Stderr was restored inline after fn(), so a t.Fatal would skip it. The plan promised `defer func(){ os.Stderr = old }()` 'and defer-closing the pipe writer', but 16cc7dc only defers the stderr restore and leaves `w.Close()` inline after fn(). That omission is exactly F15.
guidance_note: When a fix plan lists two changes, check the diff for both before replying `Fixed in`; a pipe-capture helper needs both the deferred restore and the deferred writer close.

evidence: persistent() uses a strict `> 10` and the table had only a 12-commit case; 16cc7dc adds {5,5}->recent and {6,5}->incident to pin the boundary.
guidance_note: When a threshold drives behavior, put the at-threshold and one-past cases in the table from the start.

evidence: The receive->reconcile gate is duplicated between performSyncReceive and store.SyncPull, but both call the same SyncReconcile, so the merge policy is not duplicated. 16cc7dc adds the cross-reference comment, which was one of the two options the reviewer offered.

This PR added `result.OldestDivergedUnix = recv.OldestDivergedUnix`, but the linearized arm re-reads only Ahead/Behind from fresh freshness, leaving the timestamp stale. 16cc7dc copies it from fresh as well. The plan's claim that the value would be '0 once healed' was false under the then-current SyncFreshness, which F8 exposed.
guidance_note: When adding a field to a result struct, update every branch that already refreshes its sibling fields, and check that the refreshed value really means what the plan claims.

evidence: The map[string]any payload is a pre-existing pattern across the sync payload family, and runSyncPull intercepts prose-pending before any payload is built (round-4 summary confirms the guard at sync.go:179), so there is no live bug. The pushback cited TestPrintSyncPullPayloadRejectsStrayProsePending as proof, and F10 then showed that test's name overstated what it covered. The flag is a false positive: 16cc7dc did not touch buildSyncPullPayload.

receiveInline wrote failure.blockString() to stderr itself, while a nearby comment said the surfacing decision lives with the caller. 060ed30 extracts surfaceInlineFailure(outcome, now). The change is small and makes the code match the comment, though the value is modest. The flag is a false positive: the inline rendering is original PR code.

The reviewer's framing of the ExitCode check as 'structural coupling' is wrong, since the exit code is the observable contract, and the agent said so. The redundancy was real: TestExplicitPullSurfacesContractOnProseHeld and TestSyncFailureErrorExitAndRemediation already pin it. 060ed30 drops the duplicate line.

The F4 fix (16cc7dc) copied fresh.OldestDivergedUnix on the assumption it would be '0 once healed'. SyncFreshness set it whenever ahead or behind was non-zero, so a 1-ahead/0-behind linearized result still carried a timestamp. 060ed30 gates it on `ahead > 0 && behind > 0`, which the agent says 'subsumes the round-1 linearized fix'.
guidance_note: When a fix depends on a helper returning a particular value, read that helper's population rule before claiming the value.

evidence: The reviewer concedes 'The tests do not call t.Parallel()', and Go runs a package's tests sequentially without it, so the claimed race on os.Stderr cannot happen. The flag is a false positive: the global swap is original helper code, not something 16cc7dc introduced.

TestPrintSyncPullPayloadRejectsStrayProsePending feeds status "unknown", not "prose_pending", so its name overstated what it covered. ab0593b renames it to TestPrintSyncPullPayloadSurfacesUnknownStateAsBug, which was one of the reviewer's two options. The flag is a false positive: 060ed30 touched a different test in that file.
guidance_note: Name a test after the input it actually feeds, and re-check the name whenever you cite the test as evidence in a pushback.

evidence: The doc said 'UNIX_TIMESTAMP(MIN(date)) returns an integer' while the code scans into sql.NullString and parses it; the agent says it found the decimal-string rendering mid-authoring and did not update the doc. The flag is a false positive: the stale comment predates 060ed30.
guidance_note: When an implementation discovery changes a scan type or parse path, re-read the doc comment directly above in the same edit.

evidence: The reviewer concedes 'No code path currently constructs a mixed state'. SyncFailure deliberately mirrors the flat store.UnsupportedSchemaVersionError pattern, with three constructors as the enforcement point, so turning it into a sum type would be a future-only refactor that departs from the house pattern. The flag is a false positive: the struct is original code.

The only coverage of parseUnixSeconds and earlierValidUnix was an indirect `> 0` check; the agent notes the decimal-string driver format had already surprised it once. 81fb87d adds direct table tests for both. The flag is a false positive: both helpers are original code.
guidance_note: When a parse helper exists because the driver surprised you, pin that surprise in a unit test in the same commit.

evidence: The F4 and F8 fixes cleared or refreshed the timestamp on the linearized path and in SyncFreshness. The sibling `SyncReconcileNotDiverged -> SyncPullUpToDate` arm still kept recv's timestamp, which the agent concedes is 'the one remaining path with this inconsistency'. 81fb87d zeroes it.
guidance_note: When fixing a stale field in one arm of a switch, check every sibling arm that changes the state for the same field.

evidence: The un-deferred w.Close() is the half of F1's plan ('defer-closing the pipe writer') that 16cc7dc left out. The reviewer's 'ReadAll hangs forever' is wrong, as the agent noted, because Goexit unwinds before ReadAll runs; the real residue is a leaked fd. 2e52cd5 fixes it with a concurrent-drain rewrite. The f5e0ae9 flag points at a CI-only master merge.
guidance_note: When fixing one Goexit hazard in a pipe-capture helper, apply the full idiom at once: deferred restore, deferred writer close, and a concurrent reader.

evidence: captureStderr reads the pipe only after fn() returns, so stderr output larger than the pipe buffer would block fn. 2e52cd5 adds a concurrent drain goroutine. The flag is a false positive: f5e0ae9 is a master merge of CI and Dockerfile files and the read order is original helper code. Dependence on output size is not temporal coupling, so the cited law does not fit.
guidance_note: When capturing a process stream through os.Pipe, start the reader goroutine before running the writer.

evidence: The class's own const comment says syncFailureDivergedUnresolved also covers doctor seeing a divergence with no reconcile attempted, so 'the automatic reconcile has not converged it' was false for that case. 2e52cd5 uses neutral wording rather than a Cause branch. The flag is a false positive: f5e0ae9 is a CI-only master merge.
guidance_note: When one failure class has several producers, write its message to be true for each producer listed in the class's own doc.

evidence: The reviewer concedes 'correctness is not at risk'. Freshness and Detail on doctorSyncReport are conditional in the same way, under a documented flat-struct-plus-discriminant design, so making only Age a union member would make the type less coherent. The flag is a false positive: f5e0ae9 is a CI-only master merge.

narrative: Five rounds. Two chains came from incomplete fixes. The captureStderr fix carried out only half of its stated plan (no deferred writer close), which resurfaced as F15 in round 4. The OldestDivergedUnix fix rested on a false assumption about SyncFreshness (F8), and the follow-up root fix still missed the NotDiverged sibling arm (F14). Every round also had independent findings, and the round-4 ON-POST-REVIEW flags all point at an unrelated CI master merge.
guidance_observations: The captureStderr test helper drew four findings over three rounds (F1, F9, F15, F16); applying the whole standard pipe-capture idiom at the first touch would have closed the thread in one round.
A pushback (F5) cited a test as proof whose name overstated its coverage, and the next round flagged that test; verify cited evidence before relying on it.
The OldestDivergedUnix field was patched one arm at a time across three rounds; on the first finding, walk every write site of the field.

evidence: The reviewer's drift claim between `runner.temp` and `$RUNNER_TEMP` is moot, as it concedes 'no known divergence exists'. The real kernel is the `/smoke-gocache` literal repeated four times in each workflow, under a comment citing one-source-of-truth. b473a84 writes it to $GITHUB_ENV once, because job-level env cannot read the runner context, and applies the same change to release-smoke.yml.
guidance_note: When a path literal is part of a contract shared by two workflows, define it once per workflow before copying the block from the first workflow into the second.

narrative: One advisory about a repeated cache path literal. The agent kept the real kernel (the literal was spelled out four times) rather than the reviewer's moot drift claim, and fixed both workflows. Round 2 came back clean.
guidance_observations: The repeated literal was copied from #295's release-smoke.yml; when copying a block from an earlier PR, check it for hoistable repetition before pasting.
